content: The intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of many drugs. Co-administration of certain medications with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ritonavir or lopinavir, can significantly alter drug levels and effects, leading to potential toxicity or reduced efficacy. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Palbociclib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 2. Palovarotene: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase palovarotene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Panobinostat: Both lopinavir and panobinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat prescribing information advises against combining it with QTc-prolonging drugs. 4. Pazopanib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase pazopanib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day if co-administration is necessary. 5. Pemigatinib: Ritonavir increases pemigatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 6. Pexidartinib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase pexidartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 7. Pimavanserin: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. 8. Pimozide: Lopinavir increases pimozide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Pirtobrutinib: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase pirtobrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the dose is already 50 mg/day, discontinue pirtobrutinib during strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use and resume after five elimination half-lives. 10. Pitolisant: Lopinavir increases pitolisant levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Pomalidomide: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase pomalidomide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter effects. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Ponatinib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg/day if co-administration is unavoidable. 13. Pralsetinib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Propafenone: Ritonavir increases propafenone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Quazepam: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase quazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Quetiapine: Lopinavir increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Quinidine: Ritonavir increases quinidine levels by inhibiting metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Quinine: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase quinine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Ranolazine: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Red Yeast Rice: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase red yeast rice levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Repotrectinib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-gp effects. Avoid co-administration or discontinue CYP3A4 inhibitors for 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 22. Resmetirom: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase resmetirom levels via OATP1B1/3 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Ribociclib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 24. Rifabutin: Lopinavir increases rifabutin levels, while rifabutin decreases lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 effects. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Rimegepant: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase rimegepant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-gp effects. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Riociguat: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase riociguat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or monitor for hypotension and adjust the dose as needed. 28. Rivaroxaban: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing bleeding risk. Avoid co-administration. 29. Romidepsin: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Roflumilast: Ritonavir increases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Rosuvastatin: Lopinavir increases rosuvastatin levels by decreasing metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Ruxolitinib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the starting dose to 10 mg BID with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L. 33. Selpercatinib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Selumetinib: Ritonavir increases selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the selumetinib dose as per the drug monograph. 35. Sertraline: Lopinavir and sertraline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Sevoflurane: Lopinavir and sevoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Sildenafil: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or monitor for toxicities. For erectile dysfunction, limit sildenafil to 25 mg every 48 hours with ritonavir. 38. Silodosin: Ritonavir increases silodosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 39. Siponimod: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase siponimod levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Sirolimus: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 41. Sofpironium (Topical): Ritonavir increases sofpironium levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Solifenacin: Lopinavir increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Sonidegib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 44. Sorafenib: Lopinavir increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Sotagliflozin: Ritonavir decreases sotagliflozin levels via UGT1A9 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Sotorasib: Sotorasib decreases ritonavir levels via P-gp effects. Avoid co-administration or adjust the P-gp substrate dosage. 47. Sparsentan: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase sparsentan toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or interrupt sparsentan treatment. 48. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. This combination is contraindicated. 49. Stiripentol: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase stiripentol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Ritonavir increases sulbactam levels via OATP1 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Sunitinib: Lopinavir increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Suvoverant: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase suvoverant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 53. Tacrolimus: Lopinavir increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 54. Tadalafil: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or adjust the tadalafil dose. 55. Tamoxifen: Lopinavir and ritonavir decrease tamoxifen metabolism via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 56. Tamsulosin: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 57. Tazemetostat: Lopinavir increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 58. Temsirolimus: Lopinavir increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 59. Tetrabenazine: Lopinavir and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 60. Thioridazine: Ritonavir increases thioridazine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 61. Tiagabine: Lopinavir increases tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 62. Tipranavir: Tipranavir decreases lopinavir levels, while lopinavir increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 63. Tofacitinib: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg/day. 64. Tolterodine: Lopinavir increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 65. Tolvaptan: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 66. Topotecan: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase topotecan levels via P-gp effects. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 67. Trabectedin: Lopinavir and ritonavir increase trabectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 68. Trazodone: Lopinavir increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 69. Triazolam: Ritonavir increases triazolam levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 70. Trimethoprim: Lopinavir increases trimethoprim levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. This list highlights the importance of understanding drug interactions, particularly with agents that affect CYP3A4 metabolism. Always consult prescribing information and consider alternative therapies when necessary.
